note: Wyoming State Parks recreation area on the west shore of Hawk Springs Reservoir, 13 mi N of Meriden off US-85 on Road 22 (about 10 mi N of La Grange). Sites strung along the shore road among cottonwoods, with tables and fire rings. Wyoming Game and Fish regulates boating and fishing. --Claude
summary: wyoparks page (live page refused with an F5 bot challenge; cited from the repo's 2026-10-12 capture): 24 primitive walk-up sites, 14 days in 30, seasonal water hydrants May 1-Sep 30, restrooms/playground/ramp/dock, phone 307-836-2334; not on reserve.wyoming.gov. Stored max_rig_ft 25 has no source found. Waterfront: sites along the shore road sit ~20-45 m from the full-pool water behind a continuous cottonwood band -> recommend lakefront -> lakeview.
flags: WATERFRONT (recommend lakefront -> lakeview): on Esri imagery (reservoir near full, water to the tree line) the campground is a gravel shore road running SSE from the boat-ramp area (~41.7128,-104.1955) to a small loop at ~41.7088,-104.1932, with sites on its verge and in the grassy median. A continuous band of cottonwoods ~20-30 m deep lines the whole shore between the road and the water: from the road verge at ~41.7116,-104.1941 to the water is ~29 m through that band, and the south loop (41.7090,-104.1934) is ~45 m from the water through trees. The curation rule names 'a cottonwood or tree band' between as a view; no site reaches the high-water edge over open ground. Individual site numbers could not be placed (no site map read).
